Thanks for the SIG spreadsheet you returned yesterday — the team has a few follow-ups specifically around how Redwood defines and documents the three deployment modes (Hosted, Dedicated, Private/VPC-on-prem) for SIG consumption. We want to make sure our auditors see the concrete controls that differ between the modes rather than broad marketing language.

Could you clarify:
- Tenant isolation model: how is customer separation enforced in Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
- Network/connectivity: which endpoints do we call for each mode and what are the inbound/outbound requirements?
- Key management: who controls encryption keys (Redwood KMS vs customer KMS/HSM) per mode?
- Auditability: where do audit logs live and who can access them?

If possible, a short matrix and a couple of diagrams would help the SIG reviewers short-circuit follow-ups. We have an initial SOC 2 audit kickoff in two weeks, so timely answers help.

Hi Jen —

Thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a concise matrix and a network diagram to attach — see deployment-matrix.pdf and network-diagram.png. Below is a short narrative you can paste into the SIG answers; I also flagged the cells in the spreadsheet we returned.

Quick summary (paste-friendly):
- Hosted (Redwood-managed multi-tenant): Redwood runs a shared serving fleet where logical tenant separation is enforced at the application and request-routing level. Customers have per-API key and per-tenant metadata isolation; models and KV caches are namespace-scoped. Data-in-transit is TLS only; encryption-at-rest is platform-managed with keys in Redwood KMS by default. Customers can enable customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) on an account-level contract for some enterprise plans — note: that requires Dedicated or Private in practice because of key access guarantees. Audit logs for Hosted are stored in Redwood logging backend; we provide tenant-filtered exports and can push logs to customer S3 for Dedicated/Private.

- Dedicated (customer-dedicated capacity): Dedicated provides isolated GPU pools and network isolation at the hypervisor/container level. Control plane is still Redwood-managed (API, dashboard) unless customer opts into Private. Customers on Dedicated can request private peering, and we support pushing audit logs and metrics to customer-owned storage. KMS: customers on Dedicated may configure customer KMS for model artifacts and may require an HSM-backed integration for key wrapping; otherwise Redwood KMS is used.

- Private / VPC / On‑prem: Full customer-controlled deployment model. Control plane can be run in a customer VPC or air-gapped on-prem package. Network and storage are customer-managed; Redwood provides the runtime and optional management plane. Customers retain full control of keys (KMS/HSM) and log storage. Access to logs and metrics is restricted to customer admins unless explicit support access is granted via time-limited audit sessions.

Notes on auditability & evidence:
- Hosted: we provide tenant-scoped audit exports and sampled traces; for SIG we supply exported examples and the configuration page screenshot (see attachments).
- Dedicated: we supply proof of dedicated tenancy (capacity assignment records), peering setup docs, and a sample S3 delivery manifest for logs.
- Private: provide deployment manifest, certificate of HSM integration (if used), and on-prem install checklist.

Next steps: Rishi is looped in for KMS/HSM and evidence pointers; Hannah can confirm the network endpoints in the diagram. If you want, I can convert the above into suggested phrasing for the SIG spreadsheet cells.

Best,
Kimberly Park

Hi Jen — quick technical clarifications to add to Kimberly's summary:

1) Tenant isolation specifics:
- Hosted: logical tenancy enforced by request-scoped namespace IDs and token-based access control. We use per-tenant namespaces for model artifacts and KV caches; one tenant cannot reference another tenant's namespace without explicit cross-tenant sharing which is disabled by default.
- Dedicated: isolation extends to compute and storage. Dedicated pools are assigned to a single tenant; no other customers' workloads run on those GPU pools. Control plane metadata still references the tenant for management but does not co-locate inference processes.
- Private: physical and network separation controlled by customer. Redwood runtime respects the host OS/hypervisor isolation the customer provides.

2) KMS/HSM and key-handling:
- Hosted: default keys in Redwood-managed KMS (AWS KMS or equivalent) with envelope encryption. For enterprise accounts with strict key control requirements we only offer customer-managed keys with Dedicated or Private because of how key lifecycle and rotation must be guaranteed across the serving fleet.
- Dedicated: we support customer KMS via cross-account CMKs or HSM-backed wrappers. Data-at-rest for model weights can be encrypted with customer keys; ephemeral caches may still use platform-managed encryption unless the customer requests a full key scope that we accommodate via deployment config.
- Private: customer-run KMS/HSM; Redwood never holds key material unless explicitly negotiated for managed-support engagements.

3) Audit logs & access model:
- All modes produce detailed operation and access logs. Hosted offers filtered exports; Dedicated offers both filtered exports and push delivery to customer-owned S3 or SPLUNK endpoints; Private writes to customer storage by default. For audits we provide time-limited support sessions and signed manifests showing delivery timestamps.

4) Endpoints and network requirements (high level):
- Hosted: outbound to api.redwood.example.com over TLS 443. No inbound firewall openings required.
- Dedicated: secure peering or private endpoint; inbound rules depend on peering type (we document a single port range for control-plane heartbeat + metrics egress). See attached network-diagram.png for ports.
- Private: depends on customer network; our installer documents the exact ports for runtime and management.

If you'd like, I can create a short list of SIG answer snippets (3–4 sentences per question) that you can paste directly. I started a diff of suggested edits and saved as sig-answers-diff.txt — attaching for review.

-Rishi
